previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with cirrhosis from chronic hepatitis C, hepatocellular carcinoma, and type 2 diabetes, was admitted after presenting with confusion and shakiness. Initial labs revealed hyperkalemia (K 6.2) and hyponatremia (Na 132), likely due to dietary indiscretion, spironolactone, and insulin omission. She was treated with Kayexalate in the ED, and her potassium normalized. Her confusion resolved with improved intake and glucose control. She completed a course of Bactrim for a UTI, which was discontinued. She underwent CyberKnife therapy as part of her outpatient cancer treatment plan. She was discharged on reduced-dose spironolactone, new Lasix, and continued home medications with education on low-potassium diet and symptom monitoring. Her condition was stable at discharge.
